Theme

Money, work & business · Work & responsibility

industry noun

manufacturing; a branch of business

also manufacturing, the car industry, the tourist industry, the wine industry, work in industry, industrial, industrial area, sector, business sector

modern

M-O s.v. industry (Egger)

industria quaestuōsa

noun and adjective

industry (manufacturing for profit)

Egger’s phrase, in Morgan–Owens. With quaestuōsa, money-making (Cato Agr. 1.6), it cannot be taken in the classical sense of the noun, diligence.

Other words

  • industria, industriae f. — industry, in the modern sense

    noun, first declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. industry: māchinālis industria (Egger)

    Classically diligence, hard work (ingenium industriā alitur, Cic. Cael. 45, Lewis & Short); the sense of manufacturing is modern, so on its own it can be misread.

  • quaestus, quaestūs m. — a line of business, a trade

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.150: dē artificiīs et quaestibus

    A way of making money (Lewis & Short): the classical word for an industry in the sense of a trade.

Examples

  • Jam dē artificiīs et quaestibus, quī līberālēs habendī, quī sordidī sint, haec ferē accēpimus.

    As to the trades and ways of making a living, which are fit for a free man and which are demeaning, this is roughly what we have been taught.Cic. Off. 1.150

See also business, trade, production, company.

SourcesLewis & Short: industria · Lewis & Short: quaestus · Lewis & Short: quaestuosus

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. industry.
